profile.campus: Sandston, Henrico County, Virginia (QTS Richmond 1 campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, DC5 sits at 3540 Portugee Rd, Sandston, VA 23150, part of the Richmond 1 (RIC1) campus, which totals 207 acres, 2.3 million sq ft, and 238 MW of power capacity across six buildings (DC1-DC6); no per-building MW figure is published.

QTS Data Centers (the operator name shown on this row, "Quality Technology Services," is the company's pre-2013-IPO name; it now formally operates as QTS Realty Trust and trades under the domain q.com after qtsdatacenters.com was retired) was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas. Per Blackstone's own press release, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) and other Blackstone-affiliated funds completed a roughly $10 billion acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private at $78 per share; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists its US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, placing this Northern Virginia "Data Center Alley" corridor at the center of the company's operations alongside its operations-support center in Suwanee, Georgia.

Dominion Energy, the dominant electric utility across Northern Virginia's data center corridor, has repeatedly cited data center demand growth as a primary driver of its long-term transmission and generation planning, and Loudoun and Prince William County officials have both cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a significant share of their county budgets. QTS's Virginia campuses sit within this same regional grid and policy environment as neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all tracked elsewhere in this registry.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model shared with peers like Digital Realty and CyrusOne in this same Northern Virginia corridor; under Blackstone ownership since 2021, QTS has continued expanding its US footprint (including its Manassas and Richmond 3 campuses, both still under construction as of the facts recorded here) rather than slowing development after going private.

profile.regional_context: QTS was founded in 2003 by Chad Williams, went public via IPO in 2013, and was acquired by Blackstone (via Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT) for approximately $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021, at $78/share. QTS is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Richmond, Virginia mega-campus, spanning Henrico County and Sandston. This is QTS's flagship facility story: in 2010 QTS converted a former semiconductor manufacturing site into what Wikipedia describes as a 1.3 million square foot mega data center.

reading.body:
The Sandston campus is part of QTS Richmond 1, a 207-acre property across six buildings totaling 2.3 million square feet and 238 MW of power capacity. No per-building power figure is published for DC5 itself. At typical colocation densities of 5 to 8 kW per square foot, this campus could host 11,500 to 18,400 racks assuming full IT deployment, though actual utilization depends on tenant mix and workload.

This campus ranks 24th among Virginia's 326 mapped facilities and accounts for less than 1 percent of the state's 1,375 MW of published capacity. Only 23 Virginia facilities publish power figures at all, making this campus one of a small set of transparent references for regional scale. The Richmond 1 campus sits within Northern Virginia's data center corridor alongside major operators including Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all competing for capacity on the same regional grid operated by Dominion Energy.

QTS operates as a hyperscale-neutral wholesale landlord leasing to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than running proprietary cloud services. The company was acquired by Blackstone-affiliated funds for roughly $10 billion in August 2021 and has continued expanding its US footprint after going private, with additional campuses under construction in Manassas and Richmond as of this record date. Dominion Energy and regional officials have cited data center demand as a primary driver of transmission, generation, and county revenue planning across this corridor.
